newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms but dollar rally stifles talk.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms but dollar rally stifles talk.

text.p: NWE gas oil tracked stronger crude values in early talk on Monday but a weaker mark kept key German buyers sidelined, traders said.
As jitters over the European single currency resurfaced, the mark slid almost a pfennig to a 40-month low against the dollar, making Rotterdam barges less attractive to importers.
"There's been very little physical talk. People are waiting to see what the dollar will do next and rising futures prices aren't helping," said a German trader.
Benchmark July IPE futures added $1.75 to $165.50 a tonne by 1205 GMT, lifted by Brent crude's rally on uncertainty over the resumption of Iraqi exports.
Prompt Rotterdam heating oil was valued around IPE July flat, a shade softer than on Friday, but bids and offers were around $1 apart and there was little sign of demand improving in the short-term.
Diesel premiums were little changed between July IPE +$5/+$6 a tonne fob ARA.
Cargo markets got off to a typically slow start to the week, but some traders saw signs of improving fundamentals with fewer Mediterranean barrels making their way into northwest Europe.
